sources.title: Christophe Andrieu, Arnaud Doucet, and Roman Holenstein, Particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, JRSS B 72 (2010), pp. 269–342
sources.locator: Complete 74-page author-hosted PDF. Read §§2.4.2–2.4.3, 4.3–4.5, equations (33)–(37), Theorems 4–5, and Appendix B.4. The local proofs retain only fixed-horizon exact-invariance claims and do not import the paper's separate ergodicity assumptions.

contents.name: PMMH pseudo-marginal extended target, rejection rule, and cancellation of auxiliary densities, §§2.4.2 and 4.4, equations (35)–(37), Theorem 4
contents.reason: The complete target and acceptance-ratio derivation was inspected. The local algorithm specifies the whole retained particle state and records the SMC unbiasedness hypothesis explicitly.

contents.name: PMMH extended-space invariance and exact posterior marginal, §4.4 and Appendix B.3
contents.reason: The proof route was read in full. The local proof gives the target and selected-path marginals by direct integration and applies the repository's actual general-state MH supplier.

contents.name: Conditional SMC target factorization and Gibbs updates, §§4.3 and 4.5, equations (33), (36), and Theorem 5
contents.reason: The explicit particle-system, ancestor-index, and selected-path target was inspected and reconstructed in the local item.

contents.name: Conditional particle filter and terminal-index Gibbs conditional, §4.5, Appendix A, Theorem 5
contents.reason: The conditional law and retained-trajectory index conventions were checked against the complete source section.

contents.name: PMMH and particle Gibbs fixed-N invariance claims, Theorems 4–5 and Appendix B
contents.reason: The extended-target Gibbs route was inspected; the item supplies the conditional-density cancellations locally rather than importing source acceptance.

contents.name: MCWM distinction from retained-state PMMH, §4.4 discussion
contents.reason: The difference in treatment of the current likelihood estimate was checked; the finite non-invariance witness is proved locally.

sources.retrieval_history: The complete PDF was retrieved directly from the Oxford author-hosted URL with HTTP success, extracted locally, and the cited sections and appendices were read. The browser PDF view independently exposed the same theorem and equation locations.

sources.title: Simo Särkkä and Lennart Svensson, Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2023)
sources.locator: Complete 436-page author-hosted second-edition PDF. Read §16.3.5, Parameter Estimation via Particle Filtering and Smoothing, printed pp. 340–344, including Algorithm 16.16 and the PMCMC/PMMH exactness discussion. The controlling plan's Ch. 12 locator is for the earlier edition; the current second edition relocates this material to Ch. 16.

contents.name: SIR likelihood-estimate construction and the PMMH exactness statement, §16.3.5, Algorithm 16.16 and equations (16.58)–(16.64)
contents.reason: The particle likelihood estimator and its role inside an MH update were read in the complete section. The local proof does not rely on the book's high-level exactness sentence.

contents.name: Finite-particle likelihood-based parameter estimation context, §16.3.5 and Example 16.17
contents.reason: This independent book treatment supports the scope and estimator conventions; the full invariance proof is supplied from local measure and MH arguments.

sources.retrieval_history: The full 10.83 MB PDF was retrieved from the authors' Aalto site, extracted page-by-page with MuPDF, and §16.3.5 was inspected in full.

sources.title: Fredrik Lindsten and Thomas B. Schön, On the use of backward simulation in the particle Gibbs sampler, ICASSP (2012), 25-page full text
sources.locator: Complete 25-page PDF. Read §§3.1–3.2 and 4.1, Algorithm 1–3, Propositions 1–3, and Appendix A.1–A.3. These give the backward probabilities, the explicit particle/ancestor/selected-index target, CAPF conditionals, and their algebraic derivations.

contents.name: Forward particle-system law, support condition, and backward probabilities, §§3.1–3.2 and Algorithm 1
contents.reason: The full density and the transition-density ratios used in the backward kernel were inspected; the local definition states the density and denominator hypotheses explicitly.

contents.name: CAPF and backward-simulation Gibbs updates, §4.1, Algorithms 2–3 and Propositions 1–3
contents.reason: The complete conditional auxiliary particle filter and backward simulator were read, including the distinction between backward indices and genealogical ancestry.

contents.name: Extended-target marginal and conditional proofs, Appendix A.1–A.3
contents.reason: The weight identity and conditional derivations were inspected in full and are reproduced as local proof obligations.

contents.name: Mixing motivation for backward simulation, §§1 and 4
contents.reason: The source's qualitative degeneracy discussion motivated the example, while the exact two-state transition probabilities and invariance check are calculated locally.

sources.retrieval_history: The original author-hosted people.isy.liu.se URL failed DNS resolution. Search located the same full-text paper on arXiv; the 25-page PDF was retrieved and extracted successfully. The five-retry allowance was not needed after this alternative succeeded.
